description: Consumer fixtures for rows published from evidence bundles (scripts/aggregate.mjs --from-bundles, docs/WEBSITE-HANDOFF.md). They are the producer's real output for a SYNTHETIC scenario: bundles built from the app-emitted test fixtures, published into a board holding one vendor and one legacy row. Evidence URLs name the fixture bundles' real hashes but do not resolve. tests/test_bundle_publication.py regenerates every file and fails while one differs. Every file is producer-valid (producerMustNotEmit false). The fixture sessions run synthetic copies of cpu-reference-v2 (protocol cpu-reference-v3), so configurationId cpu-reference-v2 appears with a different configurationSha256 per scenario; each hash names its own fixture file, not the committed configuration.
scenario: Google Pixel 9 / Llama 3.2 1B Q4_K_M: a verified session replaces the legacy row (--replace-legacy, kept in replacedRows); a newer failed session stays in the history and is not displayed
Google Fixture Phone / Llama 3.2 1B Q4_K_M: unverified (the configured run pins no model hash)
Google Fixture Tablet / Llama 3.2 1B Q4_K_M: failed (interrupted repetition)
Google Fixture Phone / Gemma 3 1B Q4_0 (GGUF), llama.cpp NPU: verified (accelerator-v2, gate pass, backend confirmed)

fixtures.consumerExpectation: rendered: verified, unverified, failed and vendor rows (the legacy row is replaced); build.runtimes shown; configurationId shown as the row's configuration; failed rows not shown as normal measurements
optional: history links per row key; the displayed session equals the board row
rendered like board-1.2.json; sessions without runtimeVersions give rows with no build.runtimes
